It loads original CP/M .COM/.CPM programs at 0x100 and runs Ian Collier’s Z80 interpreter, while wrappers such as zxc, zxas, zxlink, zxlibr and zxobjtohex adapt host arguments for existing compiler tools. The original release and this maintained repository are one project family, not separate records. classification.note: Cross-development tooling executes original binaries with partial CP/M 2/3 API translation. The ED FE trap routes BDOS/BIOS calls to native C; CPMREDIR maps CP/M drives and FCB operations onto host files. Required bios.bin is the bundled tiny ZXCC-specific synthetic BIOS/BDOS shim, with Z80/bios.zsm source, not an original vendor ROM or full CP/M OS. Users separately supply HI-TECH or Digital Research compiler binaries, includes, libraries and overlays.

source_cpu.note: The actual guest engine is Z80, confirmed by bin/z80.c, the shim and documentation. CP/M is the guest OS family, not a modern host target. Filename conversion enforces guest 8.3 expectations, user areas are unimplemented and unsupported BDOS calls terminate.
